name: Tristacher See
kurzbeschreibung: The Tristacher See is a picturesque lake perfect for swimming, with sunbathing areas and stunning mountain views right on the outskirts of Lienz.
preis: Kostenlos (Strandbad Eintritt ca. 6 €, Parkplatz ca. 4–5 € pro Tag)
beschreibung:
Overview

Lake Tristacher See rests as a sparkling, emerald natural jewel at an elevation of 821 meters within a forested basin at the foot of the jagged Lienzer Dolomiten, just four kilometers south of Lienz in East Tyrol. Covering roughly six hectares with a maximum depth exceeding seven meters, it is celebrated as the only natural bathing lake in the entire province of East Tyrol. Surrounded by fragrant spruce and pine woodlands, its clean, protected waters warm up during sunny summer months to delightful temperatures between 22 and 24 °C. Towering above the tree line to the south, the pale limestone towers of the Laserzwand create an awe-inspiring backdrop that captivates families, nature lovers, and swimmers. The historic Parkhotel Tristachersee graces the quiet southern bank, while the municipal lido on the eastern shore provides modern recreational amenities.

Route & Requirements

The area surrounding Tristacher See provides gentle, refreshing outings for all generations. The signature highlight is the level shoreline circuit: extending roughly two kilometers, a shaded woodland path winds through reed beds and past timber piers (walking time approx. 30 to 45 minutes, easy grade T1, fully accessible for strollers and seniors). A fascinating extension is the "Alter See" Nature and Culture Trail: branching into the protected wetland of an ancient drained lake basin, educational panels illuminate rare bog flora, dragonflies, and amphibians (1 hour loop, grade T1). Walkers from Lienz can climb through the romantic Amlach Gorge up to the lake (1 hour, 150 vertical meters, grade T1/T2). The municipal lido features expansive sunbathing lawns, beach volleyball courts, children's splash pools, and stand-up paddleboard rentals. Comfortable sneakers suffice for all paths. Leashed dogs are permitted along the forest shoreline trail, but strictly prohibited from the lido lawns and swimming waters.

Visit & Arrival

By rail, travelers arrive via ÖBB trains into Lienz station. During July and August, the complimentary municipal "Bäderbus Lienz" shuttle departs Lienz main square and railway station several times daily, traveling directly to the Tristacher See lido. Drivers reach Lienz via the B100 Drautal or B108 Felbertauern highway, following signs through Amlach or Tristach to the lake. Pay parking is available right beside the lido entrance.

Tips

Rent a stand-up paddleboard at the beach kiosk in the morning to glide across glassy water while the sheer limestone crags of the Dolomiten reflect upon the surface. In the evening, reserve a table on the waterside terrace of Parkhotel Tristachersee to savor freshly caught alpine brook trout paired with fine Austrian wines beside the water.
